lane: Full disassembly + safety/sufficiency grading of UActorPoolManager::PrimePools (rva 0x3356000), offline, s129-poolgate / merged2 / tutorial-hero images
headline: PrimePools is a clean, game-thread, no-.text-write, non-reflected native function reachable only by raw direct call — but calling it is NOT sufficient, because the enable gate is INSIDE it: vtable slot 90 resolves to the Loki override, which returns the single byte ALokiGameState+0x898 = bSupportsActorPoolPriming (measured two independent ways), so the real lever is a one-byte DATA poke on the GameState, not a call.

claims.claim: UActorPoolManager::PrimePools occupies rva 0x3356000..0x3356503 (1284 B), has exactly one ret, and every one of its 38 branches targets an address inside that range - fully accounted for, no jump-outs.
claims.evidence: `python fkdis.py d 0x3356000 1284 --dump s129` decodes cleanly; last instruction `0x03356503  c3  ret`, next byte at 0x3356504 is `ad` (unrelated). Capstone branch enumeration over [0x3356000,0x3356504): all 38 branches tagged IN, printed `total branches: 38 out-of-range: 0`. Matches the .pdata extent of 1284 B.

claims.claim: The gate site is byte-exact `ff 90 d0 02 00 00` = `call qword ptr [rax+0x2d0]` at 0x33560C5 (virtual slot 0x2D0/8 = 90, bool(this)), byte-identical in all three images.
claims.evidence: `fkdis.py x 0x33560C5 6` -> `ff 90 d0 02 00 00` in s129, merged2 AND tuthero (three runs, identical). Disasm: `0x033560BF 498b06 mov rax,[r14]` / `0x033560C2 498bce mov rcx,r14` / `0x033560C5 ff90d0020000 call qword ptr [rax + 0x2d0]` / `0x033560CB 84c0 test al,al` / `0x033560CD 7525 jne 0x33560f4`.

claims.claim: Vtable slot 90 on the base class is the universal fold `mov al,1; ret` at 0x0B9E1F0 - NON-IDENTIFYING, 26,444 occurrences of its VA image-wide. The Loki override at .rdata 0x08877A80[90] = 0x56363F0 has fold multiplicity 1.
claims.evidence: `vtables.py name UActorPoolManager --slots 96` -> `[ 90] 0x0B9E1F0`; `vtables.py name ULokiActorPoolManager --slots 96` -> `[ 90] 0x56363F0`. Raw whole-image counts of the 8-byte LE VA (unit: occurrences anywhere in the 178 MB file, any alignment): 0xB9E1F0 -> 26444; 0xF7EC20 -> 165789; 0xF7EB50 -> 27217; 0x56363F0 -> 1; 0x3356000 -> 0. claims.claim: ALokiGameState+0x898 is the UPROPERTY `bSupportsActorPoolPriming`. Two independent routes agree.

(b) Independent whole-image byte search for `C6 81 98 08 00 00 01 C3` (`mov byte ptr [rcx+0x898],1; ret`) returns EXACTLY ONE hit: 0x53800D0 - the same address. 0x898 < SizeOfOuter 0xB20.

claims.claim: bSupportsActorPoolPriming is NOT replicated and NOT config, so the live instance value is inherited from the GameState class CDO/archetype at construction.
claims.evidence: Params record at 0x8983A60: `01 00 01 00 00 04 10 00` = PropertyFlags u64 0x0010040000010001. CPF_Net (0x20) clear; CPF_Config (0x4000) clear; low word 0x0001 = CPF_Edit. Full upper-bit flag naming is [I] and nothing here depends on it.

claims.claim: PrimePools is NOT a reflected UFUNCTION and is NOT in any vtable or function-pointer table - the only invocation route is a raw direct call to rva 0x3356000 with a valid `this`.
claims.evidence: `strxref.py native "PrimePools"` -> 'no ASCII reflection name matching PrimePools'. `strxref.py find "PrimePools"` -> 3 matches, ALL UTF-16 log text (0x7F14B40 / 0x7F14BF0 / 0x7F14CB0); no standalone ASCII reflection name exists. Whole-image count of PrimePools' VA (0x7FF7BBA26000) = 0 occurrences. `fkdis.py callxref 0x3356000` = 1 site, in both s129 and merged2.

claims.claim: The single caller is 0x567AA50, inside fn 0x567A1B0 (3919 B, .pdata EXACT) which carries the ASCII literal 'ALokiGameState::BeginPlay'. Priming is designed to run once, from the GameState's BeginPlay, on a manager fetched from [GameState+0x428].
claims.evidence: `strxref.py func 0x0567AA50` -> entry 0x567A1B0, extent 3919 B EXACT, string refs include `+0xAB1 lea 0x08B2DCF8 A 'ALokiGameState::BeginPlay'` and U'Entering game state %s'. Call site: `0x0567AA41 mov rcx,rsi` / `0x0567AA44 call 0x3840490` / `0x0567AA49 lea rdx,[rbp-0x40]` / `0x0567AA4D mov rcx,rax` / `0x0567AA50 call 0x3356000`. 0x3840490 (48 B) begins `mov rax,[rcx+0x428]; test rax,rax; jne ...` - a cached-subsystem getter.

claims.claim: PrimePools runs a PRE-GATE block that re-seeds this->PoolableActorClasses (+0x88) from the class default object, and this executes even when the gate returns false.
claims.evidence: 0x3356014 `mov rbx,[rcx+0x18]` (classOff=0x18 in this build); 0x335601E `cmp qword [rbx+0x178],0` / jne / 0x335602B `call 0x1225f20` which is `mov rax,[rcx]; jmp qword [rax+0x428]` (a virtual on UClass = CreateDefaultObject); 0x3356030 `mov rbx,[rbx+0x178]` (ClassDefaultObject); 0x3356037 `lea rdi,[r14+0x88]`; 0x335603E `add rbx,0x88`; then a container copy via 0xFAF960 / 0x752A658 / 0x3352E10 over fields +0x38 (inline), +0x40 (heap ptr), +0x48 (int32 count). The gate call is at 0x33560BF, AFTER all of this.

claims.claim: The TRUE path is: re-entrancy flag -> optional slow AssetRegistry scan -> analytics virtual (slot 91) -> per-class filter loop (slot 93) -> UAssetManager::LoadAssetList async load. It needs only a CDO, a UWorld and a live UAssetManager; it allocates; it takes no locks.
claims.evidence: 0x33560F4 `cmp byte [r14+0xe9],0` -> Warning record 0x7F14BC8 'Called while priming is already in progress.' (line 165); 0x3356123 `mov byte [r14+0xe9],1`. 0x335612B `cmp [r14+0x90],[r14+0xbc]`; equal -> Error record 0x7F14C90 (line 174) + `call 0x3359d20`, which strxref shows references A'AssetRegistry', U'/Game/Loki', U'/Game/Skunkworks', U'True', U'bEnablePooling', U'GeneratedClass', U'Adding %s to list of poolable actors.'. 0x33561C7 `call qword [rax+0x2d8]` with rdx=param2, r8d=count. Loop 0x33562D6..0x3356371 calls `qword [rax+0x2e8]` per element (stride 0x30 via `lea rsi,[rax+rax*2]; shl rsi,4`). 0x3356399 `call 0x34baef0` = UAssetManager::Get (identified by U'Cannot use AssetManager if no AssetManagerClassName is defined!'), then `call rdi` where rdi=[[rax]+0x3d0], args (sret, &array, &delegate, 0x64 priority, FString U'Classes for actor pool priming' @0x7F14ED0). Result -> this+0xD8; if null -> `mov byte [r14+0xe8],1`. The only atomics are `lock xadd [rbx+8]/[rbx+0xc]` = TSharedPtr refcounts.

claims.claim: PrimePools performs ZERO module-image writes and reads no authority/role/NetMode state; its only non-stack writes are heap UObject fields this+0x88, +0xD8, +0xE8, +0xE9 - the safe DATA class on this project's hazard ladder.
claims.evidence: Full 1284-byte disassembly reviewed instruction by instruction: non-local write destinations are `mov dword [rdi+0x48], esi` (rdi = this+0x88), `mov byte [r14+0xe9],1` (0x3356123), `mov byte [r14+0xe8],1` (0x33564A0), and the TSharedPtr store into this+0xD8 at 0x3356434-0x3356451. No write to any rip-relative .text/.rdata target, no VirtualProtect-shaped pattern, and no HasAuthority / GetNetMode / role read anywhere in the body. The only world-state read is inside the slot-90 override.

claims.claim: A direct call to PrimePools alone is NOT SUFFICIENT - the gate is inside the callee, so the call still early-returns. The prerequisite is opening the gate first, i.e. GameState+0x898 = 1.
claims.evidence: Control flow: the gate call at 0x33560C5 precedes every functional block and its false arm jumps to the epilogue at 0x33564E5 (`jmp 0x33564e5` at 0x33560EF). Nothing in PrimePools' arguments or its pre-gate block can change the gate's answer, because the gate reads World->GameState->+0x898, not `this`.

claims.claim: Param2 (rdx) is dereferenced and must be a valid readable buffer of at least ~0xA8 bytes - nullptr will fault. It is consumed ONLY by vtable slot 91 (analytics).
claims.evidence: rdx is moved to r12 at 0x3356018 and consumed only at 0x33561C1 `mov rdx,r12` before `call qword [rax+0x2d8]`; r12 is then zeroed at 0x33561CD. Loki slot-91 override 0x563B170: `add rcx,0xf0; call 0x12a54a0` with rdx=param2, then `lea rdx,[rdi+0x50]; lea rcx,[rbp+0x140]; call 0x12a54a0`, then `movzx eax,[rdi+0xa0]`, `movzx eax,[rdi+0xa1]`, `mov [rbp+0x198],esi` (the count), and a timestamp double to [rbp+0x1a0]. 0x12A54A0 does `movsxd rsi,[rdx+0x48]` - an unconditional source dereference. Related shipped name A'AnalyticsActorPoolPrimingStatsEvent' at 0x887AB98.

claims.claim: PrimePools must run on the game thread.
claims.evidence: Inferred from what it touches, NOT from a thread-affinity check in the code: UClass::CreateDefaultObject via virtual slot 0x428, UE_LOG BasicLog (0x106B650), UAssetManager::Get + LoadAssetList (streamable manager), TSharedPtr construction. No `check(IsInGameThread())` was located, and DO_CHECK is 0 in shipping so its absence proves nothing.

Base vtable slot 93 = 0x335F890 = `cmp qword [rdx+8],0; setne al; ret` (the per-element filter); Loki override 0x5640390.

claims.claim: The cleanest lever is not a call at all: poke bSupportsActorPoolPriming=1 on the GameState class CDO/archetype before the world loads, so the spawned ALokiGameState carries it and ALokiGameState::BeginPlay primes naturally with the correct analytics struct.
claims.evidence: Follows from three measured facts (the property is neither CPF_Net nor CPF_Config so the instance value comes from the archetype; the gate reads the live GameState's byte; the sole caller is BeginPlay). NOT measured: that BP_LokiGameState_Tutorial_C's CDO is the archetype actually used, nor that a poke can land before construction.

claims.claim: Every page underlying these findings is decrypted in all three images, so none of it is a coverage artifact.
claims.evidence: `fkdis.py cov 0x3356000 2` -> `page 0x03356000 present` in s129, merged2 AND tuthero; same three-way check passed for the byte reads at 0x33560C5 and 0x56363F0, and `cov 0x5647000 2` -> present.

open_questions: Does opening the gate actually make SpawnPoolableActorFromClass return non-NULL? 0x566FF50 does NOT read +0x898, so 'priming is the cause of the NULL' is [I]. The bail must be inside 0x5648050 (the acquire), which I did not grade - that is the next disassembly target and it is free.

What exactly is param2 (the analytics struct)? Slot 91 reads two container/FString-shaped members at +0x0 and +0x50 (via 0x12A54A0), bytes at +0xA0/+0xA1, stores the count at this+0x198 and a timestamp at this+0x1A0. Whether a fully ZEROED ~0xA8-byte buffer is safe depends on 0x12A54A0's zero-count path, which I did not trace to its end. Untraced means unsafe to assume.

Which GameState class does the tutorial world actually use, and is its CDO byte at +0x898 zero (feature off by DATA rather than by code)? One read-only RPM on Default__BP_LokiGameState_Tutorial_C confirms the whole chain before anything is written.

Does the slot-93 filter (Loki override 0x5640390, which chains well past its 44-byte first .pdata row) reject everything on a client via bCanPrimeOnClient? If so, opening the gate yields '0 actor classes passed filtering' and priming is still a no-op. The two Display logs are free receipts that separate these outcomes, and the category's runtime Verbosity is already 4, so they WILL print.

Is [GameState+0x428] the pool-manager cache used by both call sites? 0x3840490 reads it directly and both callers pass a GameState-shaped pointer, but I only read its first 0x2A bytes (it chains past 0x38404BA).
Can PrimePools be called twice? this+0xE9 is set on first successful entry and is never cleared anywhere in the 1284 bytes, so priming is one-shot per manager instance per session.
next_experiment: Two read-only RPM reads first, zero writes: (1) read the live ALokiGameState's byte at +0x898 AND its CDO's byte at +0x898 - this confirms the gate is data-off rather than code-off and gives the reversal control; (2) read the live ULokiActorPoolManager's dwords at +0x90 and +0xBC and its byte at +0xE9 - unequal counts mean the cooked PoolableActorClasses list is present so the slow AssetRegistry scan will be skipped, and +0xE9 == 0 confirms the re-entrancy flag was never set (which the gate-false path guarantees). Only then fly the one-byte DATA poke GameState+0x898 = 1 followed by a raw direct call to 0x3356000 with a real >=0xA8-byte analytics buffer, and read the two free Display receipts ('%d actor classes found for priming.' / '%d actor classes passed filtering for this match and will be loaded.') to separate 'gate opened but filter rejected everything' from 'primed'. PRE-REGISTER: 'Feature is not enabled, skipping.' must be PRESENT at baseline and ABSENT from the post-poke call; if it reappears the poke did not land and the sitting is void.
traps_hit: Two hand-arithmetic errors, both caught, both exactly the class CLAUDE.md warns about ('recompute with a machine'). (a) I hand-added the rip-relative displacement at 0x33560CF and got .data 0x9F7FDB8, which reads ALL ZEROS and would have been written up as 'the log category is uninitialised, contradicting the observed live log'; machine recomputation gives 0x9F7EDB8, which reads `04 00 04 04` - a correctly constructed category consistent with the observation. (b) I hand-subtracted the image base from the UHT SetBitFunc VA and got 0x53500D0, which disassembles as mid-instruction garbage and would have read as 'the property record is bogus'; the correct rva is 0x53800D0, independently confirmed by a whole-image byte-pattern search for `C6 81 98 08 00 00 01 C3` returning exactly ONE hit at that address. Two further traps avoided rather than hit: `fkdis.py findptr` silently caps at 200 results so I did NOT use it for fold multiplicity (re-counted with a raw whole-file byte scan, unit stated); and the address range 0x3352000-0x3362000 contains 401 .pdata functions and is NOT one translation unit, so I enumerated the TU via its string band (`strxref near 0x07F14A40`) instead of by address range.
